UPDATE-001.summary: Resolved updates require no next-update time and display no next-update promise; active updates retain their publication requirements.
UPDATE-001.was: Every published update required a next-update time, including Resolved updates.
UPDATE-001.now: Resolved updates carry no next-update promise on any surface, including legacy resolved records with a stored time. All active-update requirements and all field, length, component, preview, review and atomicity guarantees remain.

INCIDENT-003.summary: New manual and alert-intake incidents share a durable increasing short-reference sequence while preserving every legacy reference and URL.
INCIDENT-003.was: Incident references were digits following INC- and could never be reused.
INCIDENT-003.now: Both creation paths reserve INC-n values from one durable sequence independent of legacy timestamp-sized values. Reservations remain unique across concurrency, restart, deletion and failed creation; failures may leave gaps. Existing references and URLs remain unchanged.

MAINT-001.summary: New maintenance references use an independent durable increasing short-reference sequence without changing existing references.
MAINT-001.was: Maintenance had SCH- references followed by digits and retained its separate time-window and component semantics.
MAINT-001.now: The SCH-n allocation sequence is durable and independent of incidents and legacy timestamp-sized values. Deletion, restart and failed creation never permit reuse; failures may leave gaps. All original maintenance window, component and presentation guarantees remain.

agentUpdateInstructions: The canonical source repository and edition identity are just-every/lamp. This 1.1.0 source candidate does not assert tag publication. Preserve comparison-parent and shared-component provenance at their recorded immutable revisions. Preserve the accepted public page, shared incident renderer, owner intent and customisations. Back up data and owner source; apply all listed core migrations in order and unchanged owner migrations before starting the updated Worker. Resolved updates carry no next-update promise; active updates retain every original publication requirement. Preserve existing references and URLs and retain the durable INC/SCH reservation ledger, including unused reservations. Local capture receipts are not provider acceptance or delivery; raw development envelopes and local token configuration are excluded from production builds and portable product archives. Resend remains the default; SendGrid requires explicit MAIL_PROVIDER=sendgrid and native signed-event verification or the optional authenticated relay. Preserve global_fetch_strictly_public for public Worker-hosted webhook destinations. HTTP202 remains accepted when a remote receipt is absent; this does not establish delivery. HTTP408, redirects, server failures and interruption remain uncertain and must not be automatically resent. Preserve existing SendGrid claim fingerprints and nullable actual provider receipts. Owner SQL continues after core using the unchanged lamp_ext_migrations ledger. Verify a restored copy, run full frozen-clone pnpm verify and native workflows on the exact candidate, and record the authorized source/tag and independent stage receipt separately. This candidate metadata does not assert tag publication, deployment or provider acceptance. Retain the portable authoring receipt with Git source and verify a subsequent clone using the receipt command.
